newsitem.title: UK: OECD OIL STOCKS Q2 RISE SMALLEST SINCE GULF WAR-IEA.
newsitem.headline: OECD OIL STOCKS Q2 RISE SMALLEST SINCE GULF WAR-IEA.

text.p: Oil stocks held by industry in OECD countries rose by 480,000 barrels per day (bpd) in the second quarter of the year, the smallest increase since the 1991 Gulf War, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.

The IEA said the small quarterly rise, only the third below 500,000 bpd in the last 11 years, was mainly the result of surprisingly strong demand in June and lower than expected supply from the North Sea.

"The increase in OECD industry stocks in June was much less than anticipated as strong demand and lower than expected supplies, primarily from the North Sea, compounded the expected absence of Iraqi exports and limited the monthly stockbuild to just 0.32 million bpd," the Paris-based agency said in its monthly Oil Market Report.

The IEA, which monitors oil market trends on behalf of members of the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), said falling European crude oil stocks in June offset much of a rise in refined product inventories, particularly of diesel and heating oil in the United States.
"Total North American stocks rose by a healthy 1.18 million bpd, but European and Pacific inventories fell by 0.62 million bpd and 0.23 million bpd," it said.
Stocks rose by 10 million barrels in June to 2,426 million barrels, 68 million barrels above year-ago levels but still 22 million barrels down on 1995.

Crude oil inventories are running almost exactly in line with last year's levels but stocks of products, particularly in North America and the Far East, have been swollen by rising middle distillate levels.
U.S. stocks rose by 280,000 bpd in June as refiners running flat out to meet strong seasonal demand for gasoline were also churning out unwanted diesel, heating and jet fuel.

"As a result of the gasoline-oriented refinery production, (June) stocks of middle distillates rose by 427,000 bpd and other products by 267,000 bpd, both to levels substantially above those of June 1996," it said.
Preliminary figures for July were indicating a sharp stockdraw in the U.S. as crude and gasoline inventories fell, the agency added.
In sharp contrast to the June U.S. inventory gains, European stocks fell by 625,000 bpd, led by declines in Germany and France.
Japanese oil stocks fell by 234,000 bpd, with over half the decline accounted for by inventories of non-crude refinery feedstock.
